program_overview.title: Go Programming Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The language cloud infrastructure is written in, learned the Go way: small, sharp and honest, from fundamentals to production-shaped services.
program_overview.description:
Go was designed by people tired of complexity, and it shows: a small language, a legendary concurrency story, and a standard library that ships real services without a framework safari. This live online masterclass teaches it the Go way: fundamentals fast but properly, concurrency, goroutines, channels and the patterns that make them safe, learned as the centerpiece it is, then real backend engineering: HTTP services, APIs, databases, testing as a first-class habit, and the deployment shape of production Go. A finale month ships a capstone service and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest. Small language, deep skill, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: Concurrency as the centerpiece: goroutines and channels taught with patterns and pitfalls, not just syntax
The standard library first: real services before frameworks, the way Go culture actually works
Testing as a habit from month one: table tests and benchmarks are just how Go is written
Production shape included: configuration, logging, graceful shutdown and deployment honesty
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this Go course cover?
faqs.answer: The language learned completely (it is famously small), concurrency as the centerpiece, goroutines, channels, patterns and pitfalls, then real backend engineering: HTTP services and APIs with the standard library first, databases, testing as a habit, and production shape: config, logging, graceful shutdown. A finale month ships a load-tested capstone service and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn Go properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the language and its real-world domain; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Why learn Go instead of Python or Node for backend?
faqs.answer: Different sweet spots, honestly: Python wins for data and AI glue, Node for JS-everywhere teams. Go wins where services must be fast, concurrent and operationally boring, which is why Docker, Kubernetes and most cloud infrastructure are written in it. It is also one of the fastest languages to become productive in: small surface, sharp tools, one way to format.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
